cues.text: Everything in this demo was built during the hackathon, from a fresh repo. These scenes are simulated.
A home can look fine and still block the way. For someone with a walker, who notices?
SafePath: film the home, get it measured, get the paperwork, and prove the fix.
Photos go to SAM 3.1, then a rule table, then a Muse Spark agent, then a draft subsidy package, then a re-shoot.
These demo homes ran through the real pipeline. The photos are generated and the scale is assumed, and the page says so.
SAM 3.1 finds each object from a plain text prompt. Its masks show exactly what it found.
SafePath finds the floor and draws the walking path. Shoes on the path are red. A box against the wall is only noted.
Verdicts come from a rule table, not from the model, so every number can be traced. A real A4 sheet on the door frame sets the scale. Here, it is only assumed.
Now the agent takes over. It checks low-confidence findings by looking at the photo, and it looks up the allowed items.
When it sends a value the tool won't accept, the tool refuses and the agent corrects itself. It can ask a person to check, but it cannot change a number.
The family gets a clearing list for today, and work orders.
And a draft Taiwan long-term-care subsidy package, with official item codes and caps. It stays a draft until a care professional approves it.
After the fix, shoot again. Cleared items must be gone. Construction fixes must be seen: Muse Spark compares before and after, so a missed detection can't pass as a repair.
Eleven of eleven items verified in this simulated home, each with its evidence.
SAM 3.1 sees and measures. Muse Spark does the paperwork. The code is public. See it. Fix it. Prove it.
